title: Differentiate between Primary Key and Foreign Key
summaryPoint: Primary keys enforce unique identity within a table; foreign keys build referential relationships across tables.
keyPoints: A Primary Key uniquely identifies each row (tuple) in a table and cannot contain NULL values.
A Foreign Key is a field (or collection of fields) in one table that references the primary key of another table.
A table can have only one primary key, but it can have multiple foreign keys to establish relationships with other tables.

title: Differentiate between DDL and DML SQL Commands
summaryPoint: DDL commands define and modify database structures, whereas DML commands manipulate the data stored within them.
keyPoints: Data Definition Language (DDL) commands manage the schema and table structure. Examples: CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE, DROP TABLE.
Data Manipulation Language (DML) commands insert, retrieve, and update the actual records within tables. Examples: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE.
DDL modifications automatically change structural schemas, whereas DML statements affect table contents.

title: Explain the Basic Components of a Relational Table
summaryPoint: RDBMS data representation based on relational tables made of columns and rows.
keyPoints: Table (Relation): A two-dimensional data structure consisting of rows and columns storing related information.
Tuple (Record / Row): A single horizontal row in a table representing a complete set of related data for an entity.
Attribute (Field / Column): A vertical column in a table representing a specific property or data item of the entity.

title: Explain Candidate Keys and Alternate Keys in Database Design
summaryPoint: Candidate keys are all possible unique identifiers; alternate keys are candidate keys not chosen as the primary key.
keyPoints: Candidate Key: Any minimal attribute (or set of attributes) that uniquely identifies a record in a table without redundancy.
Primary Key: The single candidate key selected by the database designer as the official unique row identifier.
Alternate Key: The remaining candidate keys that were not selected as the primary key.
